newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway names Grete Faremo energy minister.
newsitem.headline: Norway names Grete Faremo energy minister.

text.p: Grete Faremo, previously justice minister, was on Friday named industry and energy minister, succeeding Jens Stoltenberg, in the government of new Norwegian Prime Minister Thoebjoern Jagland.
Stoltenberg succeeds Sigbjoern Johnsen as finance minister. Johnsen, who has been criticised by the opposition and industry on a series of issues, becomes an ordinary member of parliament.
Faremo as justice minister emerged as a tough defender of Norway's strict immigration policies.

King Harald V appointed Jagland, 46, and his Labour minority government in a special session of the Council of State in the Royal Palace after accepting outgoing prime minister Gro Harlem Brundtland's unexpected resignation.

Stoltenberg, whose boyish charm and efficient management of Norway's oil wealth has earned him widespread popularity in opinion polls, will now manage a state budget projected to show a surplus of 40.9 billion crowns ($6.35 billion) in 1997.
"We are getting both experience and renewal in the cabinet," Jagland told reporters after being appointed.
"The policy will remain the same but I think I have a team that will be able to go out and listen to people."
